A \(180^\circ\) rotation reverses both the order of the rows and the order of the squares within each row.

Using \(\bullet\) for a shaded square and \(\circ\) for a white square, the original board is
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
\bullet&\bullet&\circ&\circ&\circ\\
\circ&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet\\
\circ&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet\\
\circ&\circ&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet\\
\circ&\circ&\circ&\bullet&\bullet
\end{array}.
\]

After a \(180^\circ\) turn, it becomes
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
\bullet&\bullet&\circ&\circ&\circ\\
\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\circ&\circ\\
\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\circ\\
\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet&\circ\\
\circ&\circ&\bullet&\bullet&\bullet
\end{array},
\]
which matches Board A.

\[
\boxed{\text{A: Board A}}
\]
